Signed-correlation knowledge-based target.

Source: R/targetGstar.R
targetGstar.Rd

The \(p \times p\) target Gstar is computed from the \(n \times p\) data matrix. It it a modified version of target G. In particular, it involves two parameters for the correlation (a positive and a negative one) instead of the single parameter \(\bar{r}\) in order to account for negatively correlated genes within the same pathway.

Usage

targetGstar(x, genegroups)

Arguments

x

A \(n \times p\) data matrix.

genegroups

A list of genes obtained using the database KEGG, where each entry itself is a list of pathway names this genes belongs to. If a gene does not belong to any gene functional group, the entry is NA.

Value

A \(p \times p\) matrix.

Details

The target uses separate mean correlations for positive and negative linked pairs: $$T_{ij} = \begin{cases} \bar{r}_+\sqrt{s_{ii}s_{jj}} & \text{if } r_{ij} > 0 \\ \bar{r}_-\sqrt{s_{ii}s_{jj}} & \text{if } r_{ij} < 0 \end{cases}$$ Here \(\bar{r}_+\) and \(\bar{r}_-\) are the mean positive and negative linked correlations.

See also

Other covariance targets: targetCor(), targetD(), targetF(), targetG(), targetGpos()

Author

Monika Jelizarow and Vincent Guillemot

Examples

# require(SHIP)
data(expl)
target_matrix <- targetGstar(expl$x, expl$genegroups)
which(target_matrix[upper.tri(target_matrix)] != 0) # not many non zero coefficients !
